主要内容: On May 4, 2022, the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced it would offer $103 billion of Treasury securities to refund approximately $47.8 billion of privately-held Treasury notes maturing on May 15, 2022. This issuance would raise new cash of approximately $55.2 billion. The securities include a 3-year note of $45 billion, a 10-year note of $36 billion, and a 30-year bond of $22 billion, all maturing on May 15, 2025, 2032, and 2052, respectively. The auctions for these securities will occur on May 10, 11, and 12, 2022, and will settle on May 16, 2022. The Treasury also plans to meet remaining financing needs through weekly bill auctions, cash management bills (CMBs), and monthly note, bond, TIPS, and 2-year FRN auctions. The Treasury anticipates reducing auction sizes for nominal coupon securities by $1 billion per month for the 2-, 3-, and 5-year notes, resulting in a $3 billion reduction by the end of July. The 7-year note auction will decrease by $6 billion, and the 10-year and 30-year auctions will also see reductions. The Treasury plans to maintain the May and June 2-year FRN auction sizes and the July new issue size. During the quarterly refunding statement on May 4, 2022, Deputy Assistant Secretary for Federal Finance Brian Smith outlined key developments in the Treasury’s financial operations. The Treasury plans to increase the size of TIPS auctions by $1 billion from the January new issue auction, aiming to stabilize TIPS as a percentage of total marketable debt outstanding. The department will continue to monitor market conditions and consider further modest increases. Additionally, the Treasury intends to transition the 4-month CMB into a benchmark bill, enhancing investor demand and operational readiness. Public transparency in secondary market transactions is being explored, with a potential request for information (RFI) to gather market feedback. The Treasury also plans to modernize auction regulations, increasing non-competitive bidding limits to $10 million. A small-value contingency auction test is scheduled for the next three months, and an LPR call is planned. These updates reflect the Treasury’s ongoing efforts to enhance market efficiency and transparency.
